PC: ABC's (must demonstrate or state that they are evaluating the airway/breathing and circulation) Asks appropriate history (a majority of the following: hx of injury, seizure, recent illness) Specifically asks about medications in the home Checks pupil size Recognizes hypoxia, begins 100% oxygen by NRB Asks for IV access to be obtained

Check bedside glucose Asks for IV naloxone (Narcan） - mg/kg dosing or 2 mg Asks for urine toxicology screen (at least) After prompted that child is not breathing, begins bag- mask ventilation with 100% oxygen

Recognizes need to intubate for airway control Orders RSI Drugs: If attempted without RSI drugs, resident will be told that the jaw is too stiff to open - still eligible for credit Atropine (0.3 - 0.5 mg) Paralytic (any ok)
Adjust bed height for intubation, position patient Gathers necessary equipment (ET Tube,laryngoscope, bag/mask - if not done at step above) Suction at bedside
Chooses proper blade size and type (Miller or Mac 2)
Chooses proper endotracheal tube size (5.0-6.0 uncuffed endotracheal tube)
Uses cricoid pressure to prevent aspiration until airway control (intubation) is achieved
Endotracheal tube passed using correct technique (credit for holding blade in correct hand, correct body position - no penalty for “breaking teeth")

Confirms endotracheal tube position: (Resident will be asked to explain his/her method(s) for confirming proper tube placement - if not offered spontaneously) Auscultates the chest Auscultates over stomach Assesses chest rise Asks for EtCO2 monitoring Orders confirmatory chest X-ray Secures endotracheal tube Places nasogastric tube (ok if prompted by “stomach is distended comment")
ICS: provide signout to the PICU fellow about this patient
